verdict.rationale: Render's own docs describe running reliable agents and background processes without wiring up queues, workers, or retry logic. Its Workflows SDKs (TypeScript and Python) let you define tasks, trigger runs from code, and chain further task runs inside a task. That covers on-demand background execution, but recurring, schedule-driven autonomy is only hinted at by a community mention of $1/mo crons, and depth is first-party claims only. Missing for 10: first-party documentation of scheduled/recurring automations (cron jobs), details on how workflow runs are triggered and monitored autonomously, and independent hands-on corroboration of workflows running in the background.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Deploy reliable agents and background processes at scale, without wiring up queues, workers, and retry logic.
The Render SDK for TypeScript provides support for: - Defining workflow tasks - Triggering runs of those tasks from your other TypeScript code
Chaining additional task runs from within a task function
